extracted.intended_audience: small biotech founders, SBIR Phase II applicants, and drug development teams preparing IND-enabling commercialization plans for an antimicrobial candidate
extracted.subtask_description: Commercialization and preclinical development planning for an antimicrobial combination therapy (ADEP4 + partner antibiotic) intended to treat MRSA and other difficult infections, with defined go/no-go criteria and regulatory strategy toward IND and clinical development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go/no-go resistance development criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The frequency of resistance development will be the go-no-go decision point for this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically, a resistance rate higher than 10^-8 is considered too high to enter development for an antimicrobial. Combinations which effectively sterilize biofilms and stationary populations of S. aureus, and have a rate of resistance development <10^-9 in the hollow fiber model will be advanced. Phase 2 will not be entered until resistance development for the combined therapeutic is conclusively demonstrated not to be a concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterilizing activity against stationary phase and biofilms (Aim 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the best sterilizing combination of ADEP4 and an approved antibiotic by examining ability to sterilize stationary and biofilm populations of S. aureus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair ADEP4 with known antibiotics (daptomycin, linezolid, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, oxacillin, etc.) and test for maximum killing of stationary and biofilm cells. Advance combinations that effectively sterilize in vitro to in vivo studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low resistance development in hollow-fiber in vitro infection model
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess ADEP4/antibiotic combinations for low resistance development using a hollow-fiber model of in vitro infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hollow-fiber model frequency of resistance as a quantitative measure; target resistance frequency <10^-9 for advancement. Compare to known examples (single-agent rifampicin/fusidic acid ~10^-8; combined treatment can be undetectable, <10^-11).

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PK/PD characterization and efficacy (Aim 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct in vivo testing of sterilizing combinations to determine PK parameters, initial efficacy, and the PK/PD driver of ADEP efficacy using mouse models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform PK and efficacy of two combinations in mice, determine pharmacodynamic driver of efficacy in a mouse model of deep-seated MRSA infection, and test efficacy in an implanted tissue cage biofilm model. Milestone: determine PK of the combined agents, the pharmacodynamic driver, and treat a previously incurable in vivo biofilm MRSA infection model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclinical toxicology studies (Aim 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform acute, dose-range finding, and 14-day repeated dose toxicity studies to support risk-benefit assessment prior to pre-IND.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct toxicity studies in rats (initially) and plan definitive GLP toxicology in two species later; use results to select human dose predictions and to support pre-IND meeting with FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genotoxicity testing (Aim 3 and GLP requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct genotoxicity assessments including Ames and chromosomal aberration tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include genotoxicity studies as part of the preclinical package; outsourced GLP genotoxicity testing should be performed as needed for IND-enabling data.

rubrics_metrics.name: GLP-compliant definitive toxicology and multi-species PK/ADME
rubrics_metrics.description: Outsource GLP studies including definitive toxicology in two species and single-dose PK/ADME studies in two species, plus bioanalytical method development and validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GLP and preclinical studies to be outsourced should include genotoxicity, bioanalytical method development/validation in 2 species, definitive toxicology in 2 species, and single-dose PK/ADME in 2 species to support IND.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety pharmacology studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform safety pharmacology studies, including CNS and respiratory assessments (in rat and additional species as required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety pharmacology assessments to be outsourced and conducted in appropriate species; include CNS and respiratory endpoints and any other regulatory-required safety pharmacology assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMP formulation, production, and stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop formulation, validate methods, produce GMP drug substance and drug product, and demonstrate stability for clinical trial materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulation development and validation, GMP production, and stability testing should be outsourced to specialists in GMP production of clinical trial materials; these activities must be documented for IND submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory strategy and FDA engagement (tier classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use FDA guidances to inform development path and engage the FDA to determine appropriate tier (e.g., Tier B vs Tier C) and necessary preclinical/clinical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft FDA guidances cited include: Developing Drugs for Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections; Early Development Considerations for Innovative Combination Products; Draft Guidance for Antibacterial Therapies for Patients With Unmet Medical Need. Expect approval to rely heavily on human PK data combined with preclinical animal data. Tier assignment depends on feasibility of studies, degree of unmet need, and strength of preclinical data — determine via conversations with the FDA and MAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product profile and indication targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the end commercial product profile (indication, route, patient and prescriber) to drive development decisions and regulatory strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualize final product and users to identify regulatory requirements and design efficient clinical trial programs. The primary objective is a product for skin and soft tissue infections; initial approval likely as a second-line treatment after failure with linezolid, with potential for first-line in immunocompromised populations. Consider additional product paths: topical nasal decolonization, creams/ointments, systemic combinations, catheter lock solutions, device coatings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial program design informed by MAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a Medical Advisory Board (MAB) and use its clinical guidance to outline clinical program design and define preclinical studies needed to support it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convene MAB composed of KOLs in infectious disease to advise on optimal use of drug combination, clinical endpoints, and trial design; MAB input will guide IND-enabling preclinical program and clinical development plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing and CRO selection with oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Outsource GLP, GMP, and specialized preclinical work to qualified CROs while providing oversight from experienced management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arietis management will choose and manage high-quality CROs to conduct GLP-compliant preclinical studies and GMP manufacturing; oversight of outsourced GLP and GMP work will be provided by the PI with 35 years' experience. Perform non-regulated basic research in-house and outsource regulated tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial and partnering strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use preclinical and Phase II data to pursue industry partnerships for development, manufacturing, marketing, and distribution; balance continued SBIR/public support with private investment and partnership decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to partner after generating preclinical data in Phase II. Consider licensing to pharma partners who can provide established marketing/distribution capabilities. Decisions about private investment, partnerships, or IPO will be data-driven based on pipeline, costs/risks, and revenue prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate unmet medical need and market potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Document clinical unmet needs (e.g., complicated SSTI, osteomyelitis, endocarditis, VAP) and market opportunity to justify development and commercial interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify market size and existing limitations of standard therapies (vancomycin, linezolid, daptomycin), show how a sterilizing antimicrobial addressing persisters could improve cure rates, reduce relapse, and command market value; use Niche Assessment and KOL/end-user input to refine product positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific benefit hypotheses to be evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate and test scientific questions regarding the benefit of targeting drug-tolerant/persister populations (e.g., shorter therapy, less resistance, causes of recurrence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Phase I/II and preclinical work to explore whether targeting drug tolerance shortens therapy, reduces emergence of resistance, and clarifies the relationship between drug tolerance, classical resistance, and biofilms; these findings may shift paradigms and support product value propositions.
